still_open.problem: New, from the C1-2 fix. _held_answer's running branch (and _wait_for_running) treats a record as a start in flight when _pid_alive(record['pid']) is False. That pid is only the group leader, but the product lock is inherited by the whole group, and stop_products signals the group with killpg. So a product whose leader died while other group members still hold the lock is now taken for a start in flight. Every env start waits 5 s and fails with 'another start of this subject is still settling', at the same commit and at another, until env stop or the checkpoint clears it. Before the fix it was answered at the same commit and replaced at another (D14). Scratch probe with run='sleep 60 & wait' and the leader SIGKILLed: with the fix, the second and third starts returned 1 after 5.1 s; the pre-fix mutant answered at once at the same commit, and at another commit stopped the group and started a new pid. A second effect: _wait_for_running never probes the lock again. If the holder dies without writing (a probe holder released the lock after 0.7 s), the call still waits 5 s and errors, where the pre-fix code at another commit took the lock and started. The new tests miss both cases because they use dead pid 999999, whose group does not exist.
still_open.proposed_fix: Judge liveness by the process group, as stop_products does. Add a helper beside _pid_alive in which os.killpg(pid, 0) succeeding means live, ProcessLookupError means gone and PermissionError means live. Use it in _held_answer's running branch and in _wait_for_running, so only a record whose group is gone, under a held lock, counts as a start in flight. In _wait_for_running, probe the product lock on each poll and return None when it is free, so the caller takes the lock and starts. Add two tests to test_env.py: (a) run 'sleep 30 & wait' and SIGKILL the leader; a start at the same commit then answers at once with exit 0, and a start at another commit stops the surviving group and starts a new product. (b) A stale running record under a holder that exits after about 0.5 s without writing; the start returns 0 well inside _STARTING_WAIT. Keep the four C1-2 tests passing, and change env-start.md's 'a record whose product is gone' to name the product's process group.
